Limitations: detection inherits DeBERTa-v3 NLI bias (alternative-backbone ablations needed for model-agnosticism); TPCG edges are pairwise (hypergraph exten- sions motivated); the benchmark is synthetic (organic-trace replication open); and α, β, θ∗ are statically tuned—adaptive calibration and cross-domain transfer are the paths to zero-shot robustness. Ethics: soft invalidation archives rather than deletes superseded chunks, preserving forensic auditability for human-in-the-loop review.

text: VI. CONCLUSION

We introduced RECONTRACE, a reference-free framework that detects and attributes hallucination and memory con- tamination in long-horizon agents. Both RQs are answered: the failures are topologically separable via TPCG Fiedler analysis (RQ1), and spectral connectivity carries actionable information about memory stability (RQ2), with a prospective protocol in the released harness. The classifier distinguishes C0–C3 with 86.4% macro F1, and an oracle-free pilot (32,562 turns) confirms the signal emerges without ground-truth labels. RECONTRACE reaches AUROC 0.942 at 64.2 ms with zero extra LLM calls, raising 100-turn task success from 63.8% to 89.2%—a principled basis for runtime epistemic auditing. The benchmark, implementation, and harness will be released publicly.
